findings.headline: Your outgoing domestic wire fee is above the market range.
findings.body: At $35, it is $10 above the $25 peer median and the highest of the 10 peers that publish it (middle half of the market: $21.25–$28.75). Wire fees fall mostly on business and higher-balance customers, the relationships most likely to compare institutions.

findings.headline: Your card replacement fee is priced below the market.
findings.body: Your card replacement fee ($7.50 vs a $10 median) sits below the peer 25th percentile. It is a customer-favorable position that peers' published schedules can verify.

findings.headline: Smaller premiums elsewhere on the schedule.
findings.body: Your stop-payment fee ($35 vs a $31 median, n=16) and your incoming wire fee ($20 vs a $14.50 median, n=16) also sit above the peer 75th percentile. Individually modest, together they shape how the schedule reads in a side-by-side comparison.

exec_narrative: Bank of the Pacific is compared with 68 banks of similar size nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index; a national set is used because fewer than 15 same-size peers in Washington have published data, so local competitors may price differently. Of 12 rankable lines, eight sit inside the middle half of the market, three above it (outgoing domestic wire fee, stop-payment fee and incoming wire fee), and one below it (card replacement fee). We would suggest one step: review the outgoing domestic wire fee, which sits above the market range; the peer median of $25 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Outgoing domestic wire fee — $35
callouts.stat: Peer median $25 · middle half $21.25–$28.75 · range $15–$35 · 100th percentile · n=10
callouts.body: Published as “Outgoing domestic wire transfer (branch).” At $35 it is $10 above the $25 peer median. Wire fees fall mostly on business and higher-balance customers, the relationships most likely to compare institutions. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $25 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Incoming wire fee — $20

callouts.body: Published as “Incoming wire transfer.” At $20 it is $5.50 above the $14.50 peer median. Charging to receive funds is increasingly uncommon and is noticed by business customers. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $14.50 is the reference point.

callouts.body: Published as “Replacement card.” A customer-favorable price on a low-volume line. No action is indicated unless it is an old price that was never revisited, in which case the peer median of $10 is the reference point.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Bank of the Pacific with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
